filler.note: 5 of the 7 new pages measured are shop pages. Until the shop is connected to your Square catalog they show made-up sample products with Latin names and prices nobody charges, none of them yours, so for those pages the figures compare the page itself, not the products on it.

rows.label: Wait before the page shows on a phone
rows.why: Visitors see your page in 0.9 s instead of 15.2 s.
rows.impact: People leave a slow page before they reach your shop or your party booking.
rows.fine: Largest Contentful Paint, mean of 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them; 0 of 8 within 2.5 s today, 7 of 7 rebuilt.

target.label: Good
target.source: Google’s Core Web Vitals mark for a good page load (web.dev).

rows.label: Speed on a phone, out of 100
rows.why: Most people look up a studio on their phone first.
rows.impact: This is their first impression of you.
rows.fine: Google Lighthouse performance score, mean of 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them.

target.label: Good
target.source: The green “good” band of Google Lighthouse’s score (Chrome developer docs).

rows.label: Data a phone downloads per page
rows.why: Less to download means the page opens faster on a weak signal and costs visitors less data.
rows.fine: Total transfer size, mean of 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them; 129 files a page today, 8 rebuilt.

rows.label: Usable by every visitor, out of 100
rows.why: An accessibility scanner found 90 problems on these pages today, and none on the new ones.
rows.fine: Google Lighthouse accessibility score on phones, mean of 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them; axe-core WCAG 2.2 A and AA failures on desktop.

target.label: Good
target.source: The green “good” band of Google Lighthouse’s score (Chrome developer docs).

rows.label: Ready for Google, out of 100
rows.why: Nothing basic is missing when Google decides how to list you.
rows.fine: Google Lighthouse SEO score on phones, mean of 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them.

target.label: Good
target.source: The green “good” band of Google Lighthouse’s score (Chrome developer docs).

rows.label: Pages a visitor can zoom in on
rows.why: Some visitors need to pinch to enlarge the text before they can read it.
rows.fine: Pinching to enlarge text on a phone, which some visitors need to read it. Measured on 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them.

target.label: Goal
target.source: No published benchmark; every page is the natural goal.

rows.label: Pages with a summary for Google results
rows.why: The short description Google may show under your name.
rows.fine: The short summary Google may show under the page’s title. Measured on 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them.

target.label: Goal
target.source: No published benchmark; every page is the natural goal.

rows.label: Pages with details Google can read directly
rows.why: Facts about you and what you sell, in the structured form Google reads for its results.
rows.fine: Structured data (JSON-LD) of any kind on the page. Measured on 8 current pages against the 7 new pages that replace them.

target.label: Goal
target.source: No published benchmark; every page is the natural goal.

rows.label: Your facts readable without running scripts
rows.why: Your current pages draw every word with a script, and many AI tools and crawlers do not run scripts.
rows.impact: They now see what a visitor sees: your hours, address and party packages.
rows.fine: Page text with JavaScript off. Share of 85 checks of 56 facts about the studio, on the same pages.

rows.label: Your facts AI assistants can read directly
rows.why: AI assistants answer questions about studios like yours, and can quote your details instead of guessing them.
rows.fine: Structured data (JSON-LD). Share of 85 checks of 56 facts about the studio, on the same pages.
